Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise, clinician-ready historical checkpoint note for my rehabilitation archive summarizing the evidence reviewed on February 19, 2027, that supported advancement beyond the initial 20-minute run-walk restart stage. Include the completed session count, session structure, spacing, and both during-session and following-day symptom checks. Clearly frame this as prior advancement evidence, not as current clearance.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical rehabilitation checkpoint — February 19, 2027", "body": "## Historical checkpoint — reviewed February 19, 2027

**Purpose:** Record the evidence supporting advancement beyond the initial 20-minute run-walk stage. This is historical documentation of the February 19 review, **not current clearance or a statement of present status**.

- **Completed:** Six sessions — January 26, January 30, February 2, February 6, February 10, and February 13, 2027.
- **Structure:** Each session was 20 minutes, alternating 4 minutes of easy running with 1 minute of walking.
- **Spacing:** Sessions were nonconsecutive; the plan was limited to two sessions per week.
- **During-session and later-that-day checks:** All six sessions were documented without focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change.
- **Following-day checks:** Each following day was documented as symptom-free, including ordinary walking and stairs.

At the February 19 clinical review, this six-session record supported the then-documented step to two nonconsecutive 25-minute sessions per week, alternating 9-minute easy runs with 1-minute walks. That review required six symptom-free sessions at the 25-minute level before continuous running; the former 40-minute baseline remained suspended. These are the limits recorded at that historical review and do not establish current authorization.", "folder": "Rehabilitation archive"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_087_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document states that six sessions were completed, that they were nonconsecutive, that each session lasted 20 minutes, and that each used alternating four-minute easy runs with one-minute walks. Missing or contradictory count, duration, spacing, or interval structure must fail.

The document states that every completed session and every corresponding following day remained free of focal pain, swelling, instability, and gait change. It must cover both the during-session and following-day observations; omissions or contradictions must fail.

The document is clearly framed as a concise clinician-facing historical checkpoint describing prior evidence that supported advancement beyond the initial 20-minute restart stage at the February 19, 2027 review. It must not present this checkpoint as current clearance or a current tolerated running level.", "value": {"title": "Historical rehabilitation checkpoint — February 19, 2027", "body": "## Historical checkpoint — reviewed February 19, 2027

**Purpose:** Record the evidence supporting advancement beyond the initial 20-minute run-walk stage. This is historical documentation of the February 19 review, **not current clearance or a statement of present status**.

- **Completed:** Six sessions — January 26, January 30, February 2, February 6, February 10, and February 13, 2027.
- **Structure:** Each session was 20 minutes, alternating 4 minutes of easy running with 1 minute of walking.
- **Spacing:** Sessions were nonconsecutive; the plan was limited to two sessions per week.
- **During-session and later-that-day checks:** All six sessions were documented without focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change.
- **Following-day checks:** Each following day was documented as symptom-free, including ordinary walking and stairs.

At the February 19 clinical review, this six-session record supported the then-documented step to two nonconsecutive 25-minute sessions per week, alternating 9-minute easy runs with 1-minute walks. That review required six symptom-free sessions at the 25-minute level before continuous running; the former 40-minute baseline remained suspended. These are the limits recorded at that historical review and do not establish current authorization.", "folder": "Rehabilitation archive"}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_087_01","passed":false,"reason":"The session count, nonconsecutive spacing, 20-minute duration, 4-minute run/1-minute walk structure, and historical-not-current framing are present. However, the following-day check says only that each day was “symptom-free, including ordinary walking and stairs”; it does not explicitly document absence of focal pain, swelling, instability, and gait change on every following day as required."}]}
